issues.body: The diff repeatedly says the one-`save-if` posture is pinned by `scripts/tests/test_mergequeue_cache_posture.py`, but that test's `with_value` helper returns the first matching key and never rejects a second non-comment key. Thus the duplicate-key regression found in round 1 would still pass. This is materially the same minor finding as round 2.
issues.fix_hint: Extend the structural posture test to count non-comment `save-if:` entries in every rust-cache `with:` mapping and assert that the count is exactly one; alternatively narrow the comments so they do not claim key uniqueness is pinned.
issues.title: Cited posture test still does not pin mapping-key uniqueness

verdict.summary: Round 3 leaves the workflow correction internally consistent: the affected rust-cache mappings each contain one main-only `save-if`, and the coverage measurement shards share `coverage-measure` without claiming workspace artifacts are cached. The prior minor finding remains unchanged: the newly repeated statement that `scripts/tests/test_mergequeue_cache_posture.py` pins this posture is stronger than the test, because `with_value` returns the first matching key and does not reject duplicate non-comment keys. The exact duplicate-key regression from round 1 would therefore still pass. This is a test-coverage/documentation precision gap rather than a defect in the corrected workflow, so approval remains appropriate.
